swapped.why: Dinah is Jacob's only named daughter, and nearly every Bible fact about her names her as his daughter or his sons' sister, so there aren't 7 different medium-hard clues that avoid giving her away.

clues.text: At the gateway of Hebron, he pulled Abner aside as if to talk privately, then stabbed him.
Finding Absalom still alive and caught in an oak tree, he thrust three spears through his heart.
Following King David's letter during the siege, he placed Uriah the Hittite where the strongest enemy soldiers were.
David promised command to whoever first struck down a Jebusite, and this man went up first and became chief.
After backing Adonijah against Solomon, he fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
Seeing that King David longed for Absalom, he sent to Tekoa for a wise woman to pose as a mourner.
While pursuing Sheba son of Bichri, he caught Amasa off guard and stabbed him with a dagger.
At Ramoth-gilead, a young prophet poured oil on this army commander's head, anointing him king over Israel.
The watchman on the tower at Jezreel said this charioteer was driving like a madman.
On Naboth's land near Jezreel, he drew his bow and shot King Joram of Israel between the shoulders.
He looked up at a window in Jezreel and shouted to the eunuchs to throw Jezebel down.
He wrote letters to Samaria, and its leaders sent him the heads of Ahab's seventy sons in baskets.
He called a great sacrifice for Baal, but it was a trick to gather and destroy all of Baal's servants.
For destroying the house of Ahab, the LORD promised four generations of his sons would sit on Israel's throne.
King Saul was pleased to hear that this daughter of his loved David, hoping she would become a snare to him.
Saul gave her to David in marriage after David brought him two hundred Philistine foreskins.
When Saul's messengers watched David's house to kill him in the morning, his wife let him down through a window.
To fool Saul's men, she laid a household idol in David's bed with goat hair on its head.
When Ish-bosheth took her back for David, her husband Paltiel followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim.
As the ark entered the City of David, she watched King David dancing from a window and despised him.
After scolding King David for uncovering himself before the maidservants, she had no children to the day of her death.
A new king ignored the elders who had served his father and took advice from the young men he grew up with.
Asked to lighten Israel's heavy yoke, this king said his father used whips, but he would use scorpions.
After Shishak of Egypt carried off Solomon's gold shields, this king of Judah made bronze shields to replace them.
Israel stoned Adoram, the king's man over forced labor, and the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem.
He gathered 180,000 warriors of Judah and Benjamin, but Shemaiah told them not to fight their brothers.
This king of Judah had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, but loved Maacah daughter of Absalom most.
This king reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, and his mother was Naamah the Ammonite.
On a road outside the city, the prophet Ahijah tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and told this man to take ten.
This king made two golden calves and set one in Bethel and the other in Dan.
At the altar in Bethel, this king's hand withered when he stretched it out to seize a man of God from Judah.
When King Solomon sought to kill him, this man fled to Shishak king of Egypt and stayed until Solomon died.
This king sent his wife in disguise to the old, blind prophet Ahijah to ask about their sick son.
Seeing this young Ephraimite servant was industrious, Solomon put him over the labor force of the house of Joseph.
This king of Israel built shrines on the high places and appointed priests from every class of people who were not Levites.
This king of Tyre sent cedar logs, carpenters and stonemasons to build King David a palace.
When Solomon asked for cedars for the temple, this king rejoiced and blessed the LORD for giving David a wise son.
This king promised to float cedar and cypress logs to Solomon as rafts by sea, asking for food in return.
Solomon gave this king twenty towns in Galilee, but he was not pleased and called them the Land of Cabul.
This king sent sailors who knew the sea to serve in Solomon's fleet at Ezion-geber, which brought gold from Ophir.
This king's fleet brought almug wood from Ophir, which Solomon made into lyres and harps for the singers.
This king of Tyre sent Solomon a craftsman whose mother came from the daughters of Dan, skilled in gold, bronze and engraving.
A ruler had John the Baptist arrested, bound and put in prison because of this woman, Philip's wife.
John the Baptist kept telling the king it was not lawful for him to have this woman, his brother's wife.
This woman held a grudge against John the Baptist and wanted to kill him.
John the Baptist rebuked the tetrarch over this woman and over all the other evils he had done.
This woman's chance against the Baptist came at the king's birthday banquet for the leading men of Galilee.
At the king's birthday banquet, this woman's daughter danced and pleased him and his guests.
When her daughter asked what to request from the king, this woman answered, "The head of John the Baptist."
Leah named her second son this, saying the LORD had heard that she was unloved.
He and Levi took their swords into Shechem while its men were still in pain and killed every male.
In Egypt, Joseph took this brother away from the others and had him bound before their eyes.
Joseph's steward told the brothers not to fear over the silver in their sacks, then brought him out to them.
Blessing his sons, Jacob said this son and Levi were brothers whose swords were weapons of violence.
When Joshua divided the land, this son's tribe got its inheritance inside Judah's territory, since Judah's share was too large.
Moses said this son's tribe would stand on Mount Gerizim with Levi, Judah and others to bless the people.
Leah named her third son this, hoping her husband Jacob would at last become attached to her.
With his brother Simeon, he took a sword into Shechem and killed its men to avenge their sister Dinah.
Among the sons of Jacob who went down to Egypt, this one fathered Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
In Egypt, the parents of the baby Moses, hidden in a basket by the Nile, both came from this family line.
When twelve tribal staffs were placed in the Tent of Meeting, this tribe's staff, bearing Aaron's name, sprouted almonds.
In the wilderness, the LORD set this tribe apart to carry the ark of the covenant and pronounce blessings.
When Moses gave out land to Israel's tribes, this tribe got no territory, for the LORD was its inheritance.
In the wilderness, Dathan and Abiram of Reuben joined his followers in rebelling against Moses and Aaron.
In the wilderness, the earth opened its mouth and swallowed this rebel's men, their households and all their possessions.
Fire came from the LORD and consumed the 250 men of his group who were offering incense.
Moses told this Levite that the tabernacle work was not enough for him, since he sought the priesthood too.
Eleazar had his followers' bronze censers hammered out to overlay the altar, a reminder that only Aaron's descendants offer incense.
Psalm headings credit his sons with songs, including the one that begins, "As the deer pants for streams of water."
Jude warns of false teachers who followed Cain, rushed into Balaam's error, and perished in his rebellion.
While this king of Judah raged at the priests in the temple, leprosy broke out on his forehead.
In the year this king died, Isaiah saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted.
He became king of Judah at sixteen and reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years.
Priests stood against this king, saying only Aaron's descendants were set apart to burn incense to the LORD.
Fighting the Philistines, this king of Judah tore down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod.
This king of Judah had devices made in Jerusalem to shoot arrows and hurl large stones from the towers.
Zechariah foretold a flight like the people's flight from the earthquake in this Judean king's days.
This king of Judah removed his grandmother Maacah as queen mother because she had made an Asherah pole.
Facing a vast Cushite army, this king of Judah prayed, 'Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on You.'
This king of Judah sent a gift of silver and gold, asking a foreign king to break his treaty with Baasha.
Angry at a seer's rebuke, this king of Judah put him in prison and oppressed some of the people.
Late in his reign, this king of Judah became diseased in his feet but sought only physicians, not the LORD.
This king of Judah had his men carry off Baasha's stones and timbers from Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah.
A prophet met this king and all Judah and Benjamin, saying, 'The LORD is with you when you are with Him.'
After Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground, Joshua set up twelve stones from the river at this camp.
God told Joshua that here He had rolled away the reproach of Egypt, and the place was named for it.
Camped here on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites kept the Passover soon after entering Canaan.
After Saul defeated the Ammonites, Samuel led the people here to confirm Saul as king before the LORD.
Waiting seven days here for Samuel while his troops deserted, Saul offered the burnt offering himself.
Samuel hacked Agag king of the Amalekites to pieces before the LORD at this place.
During a famine here, Elisha threw flour into a pot of deadly stew cooked for the sons of the prophets.
Abram came to the Oak of Moreh at this place, and the LORD promised the land to his offspring.
Jacob bought the plot of ground where he camped here from the sons of Hamor for a hundred pieces of silver.
To avenge their sister Dinah, Simeon and Levi slaughtered every male of this city while the men were still in pain.
The bones of Joseph, brought up from Egypt, were buried at this place on land Jacob had purchased.
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel here, made a covenant, and set a large stone under an oak.
Abimelech captured this city, killed its people, demolished it, and sowed it with salt.
After Solomon died, Rehoboam went to this place because all Israel had gathered there to make him king.
Grieving for his people, Jeremiah asked if there was no balm here and no physician.
Jacob fled from Laban toward these hills, and Laban chased him seven days to catch him there.
Joseph's brothers saw an Ishmaelite caravan coming from here, carrying spices and myrrh down to Egypt.
The Reubenites and Gadites, who had very large herds, saw this land was good for livestock.
Its men held the Jordan fords and made fleeing Ephraimites try to say Shibboleth.
Elijah the Tishbite, who told Ahab there would be no dew or rain, was among its settlers.
In the Song of Solomon, the bride's hair is like a flock of goats streaming down its mountain.
Naboth owned a vineyard in this place, right next to the palace of King Ahab.
When Jehu arrived at this city, Ahab's queen painted her eyes and looked down from a window.
As heavy rain fell, Elijah tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot all the way here.
Before Gideon blew the ram's horn, the Midianites and Amalekites crossed the Jordan and camped in this valley.
While the Philistines gathered their forces at Aphek, Israel's army camped by the spring at this place.
Wounded by the Arameans at Ramah, King Joram son of Ahab came back to this city to recover.
The seventy sons of Ahab were slaughtered, and their heads were sent in baskets to Jehu at this city.
Rachel named Bilhah's first son this, saying God had vindicated her and heard her plea.
Jacob blessed this son as a snake by the road, a viper biting the horse's heels.
In his final blessing on the tribes, Moses called this tribe a lion's cub leaping out of Bashan.
King Jeroboam set up one golden calf in Bethel and the other in this northern city.
All Israel, from this city to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet.
The city once called Laish was renamed after the forefather of the people who settled there, a son of Israel.
Samson's father Manoah, a man of Zorah whose wife was barren, came from the clan of this tribe.
After praying for His followers, Jesus led His disciples across this valley and into a garden.
As King David left Jerusalem and crossed this valley, the whole countryside wept loudly.
King Solomon told Shimei to stay in Jerusalem, warning that crossing this valley would mean his death.
King Asa removed his grandmother Maacah as queen mother and burned her Asherah pole in this valley.
King Josiah burned the temple's Asherah pole in this valley, ground it to powder, and threw the dust on graves.
In King Hezekiah's day, the Levites carried the unclean things cleared from the temple out to this valley.
Through Jeremiah, the LORD promised that the fields stretching as far as this valley would be holy to Him.
During a violent storm at sea, frightened sailors used these to find out who was to blame, and Jonah was picked.
When these were used to choose, the choice fell to Matthias, so he was added to the eleven apostles.
At the cross, soldiers chose not to tear Jesus' tunic and used these to decide who would get it.
On the Day of Atonement, Aaron used these over two goats to choose one for the LORD and one as the scapegoat.
At Shiloh, Joshua used these in the presence of the LORD to share out the land among the remaining tribes.
In Nehemiah's day, the people used these to pick one out of every ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city.
The temple gatekeepers, young and old alike, used these to decide which gate each family would guard.
At Moses' census, each man paid half of one; the rich could not give more, nor the poor less.
Elisha foretold that at Samaria's gate, a seah of fine flour would sell for just one of these.
While hunting lost donkeys, Saul's servant offered a quarter of one in silver to pay the man of God.
When the Philistines sharpened Israel's tools, the charge for an axe or pitchfork was a third of one.
Moses collected five of these for each firstborn Israelite beyond the number of the Levites, to redeem them.
Joseph's brothers pulled him from the cistern and sold him to traders bound for Egypt for twenty of these in silver.
Amos condemned merchants who wanted to shrink the ephah, make this bigger, and cheat with dishonest scales.
On the Day of Atonement, Aaron laid both hands on a live one and sent it into the wilderness.
Joseph's brothers slaughtered one and dipped his robe in its blood before sending the robe to Jacob.
In a vision beside the Ulai Canal, one charged a two-horned ram and shattered both its horns.
In Jesus' parable, the older son complained that his father never gave him a young one to celebrate.
Judah promised Tamar a young one from his flock and left his seal, cord, and staff as a pledge.
To fool Saul's messengers, Michal put its hair on a household idol lying in David's bed.
When the Son of Man judges the nations, He places the sheep on His right and these on His left.
The law of Moses said not to muzzle this animal while it was treading out the grain.
Driven away from mankind, King Nebuchadnezzar ate grass like this animal, drenched with the dew of heaven.
Through Isaiah, God said this animal knows its owner, but His people Israel do not know Him.
Jesus asked the Pharisees which of them would not pull out a son or this animal fallen into a pit on the Sabbath.
At Sinai, God commanded Israel not to covet a neighbor's house, wife, servants, donkey, or this animal.
In Ezekiel's vision, each living creature had the face of a man, a lion, an eagle, and this animal.
Under the law given through Moses, if this animal gored a man or woman to death, it was stoned.
